rows.why: Item 1 asks which units are accepted. Its pick accepts d, h, m, s and ms, so `2d` and `1d0h0m0s0ms` parse as the scenario expects.
Item 4 asks whether whitespace is allowed. Its pick strips leading and trailing whitespace, so "  45m\n" parses to 2700000.

This scenario mixes several questions. Item 6 covers the most rows (`1.5h`, `-3s`, `+3s`, the full-width digit `３s`, and `1_0s`), and its ASCII-digit-only pick rejects all of them. Other rows belong to items 7 (empty), 5 (`90`), 4 (spaces), 2 (`3S`) and 10 (`05s`). Item 10's pick, which accepts leading zeros, would conflict with the `05s` row.
No item asks whether a count may be larger than the next unit up (e.g. `90m`). Item 3 is about order and repetition, not a count's size.
Item 3 asks about unit order and repetition. Its pick rejects out-of-order and repeated units, matching every row.
Item 8 asks about the upper limit. Its pick rejects only totals above 9007199254740991, so that exact value parses.
Item 8's pick rejects totals above 9007199254740991 ms and rejects very long digit strings early, which covers both rows.

Item 11 asks how milliseconds are formatted. Its pick chooses the shortest string, giving `90s` for 90000 and `90m` for 5400000, but the scenario expects `1m30s` and `1h30m` (largest units first). Item 9's pick also formats 0 as `0s` where the scenario expects `0ms`.
Under item 11's shortest-string rule, `9007199254740991ms` (18 characters) beats `104249991d8h59m991ms` (20 characters), so the pick would not give the expected output.
No item asks whether formatting then parsing returns the original number. Any format that parses correctly passes, so no single item's answer settles it.
Item 12 asks what format_duration does with invalid input. Its pick raises a ValueError mentioning 'milliseconds' for negatives, values above the maximum, floats and bools, matching every row.
